title: Lightning mobile SDK onramp playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose
---
Working draft: a tiny, frictionless mobile SDK onramp aimed at shipping an end-to-end first-run in under 10 minutes for iOS and Android teams. Focus: minimal gradable surface (size, auth, network edge cases), clear debugging hooks, and observability baked in.

Context and problem statement
- Mobile apps need a tiny dependency, predictable binary size, minimal runtime setup, and strong offline/fallback behavior.
- Current SDK examples are desktop-first, rely on long-lived env vars and developer keys, and assume background processes that mobile can't replicate.
- Goal: reduce time-to-value for an engineer who wants to add a single call (e.g., summarize user text) with safe defaults and a path to production.

Guiding constraints (priorities)
1) Binary size: < 250KB additional on app binary for core networking + minimal serializers (strip debug).
2) Auth: short-lived tokens pattern + easy KMS handshake; no embedding of long-lived keys in app.
3) Network: conservative retry and offline caching strategy; graceful degradation to local fail message.
4) UX: single-file quickstart with copy-paste sample for iOS Swift and Android Kotlin.
5) Observability: events emitted to a lightweight telemetry API (opt-in during dev).

Quickstart outline (10-min path)
1) Add dependency
   - iOS: Swift Package URL + import RedwoodMobile
   - Android: maven coordinate + implementation 'ai.redwood:mobile-sdk:0.1.0-beta'
2) Initialize SDK with ephemeral key exchange
   - recommend flow: app requests ephemeral token from backend (backend calls Redwood token API). Provide sample server snippet (Node/Python) in repo.
3) Make a single call (text summarize)
   - copy/paste-ready call in 6 lines (example code included in repo sample files).
4) Toggle streaming on/off (dev-only)
5) Verify response and display results in a minimal view
6) Enable telemetry (optional) and view sample events in the Console

Minimal sample code (inline pseudocode)
- iOS Swift (very small)
  let ephemeral = await fetchFromAppBackend("/ephemeral")
  let client = RedwoodClient(token: ephemeral.token)
  let resp = try await client.generate(prompt: "Summarize: \"...\"", maxTokens: 60)
  label.text = resp.text

- Android Kotlin (very small)
  val ephemeral = http.get("/ephemeral")
  val client = RedwoodClient(ephemeral.token)
  val resp = client.generate("Summarize: ...", maxTokens = 60)
  textView.text = resp.text

Auth best-practices (mobile)
- Never ship long-lived API keys in the app.
- Backend should mint ephemeral tokens with a 60–300s TTL for dev/test. Production: use mTLS or signed JWTs with short TTLs.
- Local dev: provide a CLI helper to create ephemeral tokens locally to speed iteration.

Network & caching policy
- Primary: fetch with 3s connect timeout, 10s overall deadline for small prompts.
- Retries: idempotent GET-style health calls: 1 retry, generation calls: no automatic retry by default (risk of double-charge), expose retry helper that callers opt into.
- Offline cache: store last-successful summarized text per user action key (LRU, 5 items, TTL 24h). On network fail, surface cached item and "stale" badge.

Observability hooks (what to surface)
- Event types: sdk.init, call.start, call.finish, call.error, cache.hit, auth.refresh.
- Minimal payload: event_name, timestamp, region, model_id, latency_ms, token_renewal_status, error_code. No PII.
- Allow dev to opt-in to telemetry for early testing; default OFF.

Debugging toolbox (for developers)
- Local proxy CLI: logs requests/responses, rewrites endpoints to staging.
- On-device verbose mode (dev-only) that logs events to a file reachable via Xcode / adb.
- SDK exposes internal state inspector (memory-light): current token expiry, last-call-id, pending-kv-cache-keys.
- Common failure symptoms mapping:
  * 401 on init -> backend token exchange failing; suggest checking backend env and time sync.
  * 504 long wait -> optimistic timeout too small; advise increasing per-route deadline.
  * empty / partial streaming -> check model compatibility for streaming on that route.

Rollout & gating plan
- Alpha (internal): framework-only release to 5 apps, smoke tests for init, basic generate, telemetry events present. (2 weeks)
- Beta (customer opt-in): invite select customers, gather crash and latency metrics, ABI/packager feedback. (3–4 weeks)
- GA: enable in console templates and docs with migration notes. (post-beta)

Metrics for success (first 90 days)
- Time-to-first-successful-call (median) < 10 minutes for new devs following quickstart
- Crash rate attributable to SDK < 0.05% active installs
- Average added app binary size (MB) <= 0.25MB
- Rate of successful ephemeral token exchanges > 99%

Open questions / tradeoffs
- How aggressive should the offline cache be? privacy concerns vs UX. Propose opt-in per app by default-off.
- Streaming support: do we implement full incremental UI primitives or provide basic event stream with example scaffold? (lean: scaffold only for v1)
- Binary size: shipping proto vs json parsers — which wins in real installs? run A/B with two samples.

Repo and samples to include
- /samples/quickstart/ios/simple-summarize (app folder, copy-paste friendly)
- /samples/quickstart/android/simple-summarize
- /samples/server/ephemeral-token-exchange (node + python)
- /tools/local-proxy (node cli)
- README: step-by-step checklist for QA + release notes template

Next actions (owner: Aisha)
- [ ] Prototype Swift Package + Kotlin artifact (due 2025-01-22)
- [ ] Wire up ephemeral-token-exchange sample (due 2025-01-24)
- [ ] Build local-proxy with recording mode (due 2025-01-28)
- [ ] Internal alpha release to 5 apps and collect runbook feedback (due 2025-02-05)

Notes to self / rough ideas
- Consider a tiny webview-based sample to demo quick UI for streaming without native plumbing.
- Add a "billing guardrail" in examples: how to detect runaway generation costs and auto-disable network calls in debug.
- Keep the docs conversational and copy-paste-first.

Unresolved
- Decision: default telemetry opt-in vs opt-out for internal devs. (flag needed in console?)
- Finalize token TTL recommendation for production (mTLS vs signed JWT).

References and inspirations
- Chrome's offline caching patterns, Firebase Auth ephemeral flows, and common mobile SDK telemetry contracts.

---
Rough authoring notes: this is intentionally terse and action-oriented. We'll expand each sample into a concrete README and add CI smoke tests before beta.
